summary: Backend-only validation of the Heavy-Logistics (Camión) quote flow with Option B admin WhatsApp alert. 5/5 pytest cases GREEN. Full flow exercised end-to-end against preview backend: (1) GET /api/public/cities → 200 with cities array; (2) admin badarbox1756@gmail.com logs in and /api/auth/me confirms role='admin' AND phone='+34612284215' (matches seed_admin.py); (3) customer qa_customer@nubo.com creates POST /api/orders/logistics-quote → 200, order_type='logistics', status='pending_quote', total_amount=0, vehicle_type='truck'; (4) PATCH /orders/{id}/set-quote-price authorization matrix verified — customer→403, total_amount=0→400, total_amount='abc'→400, admin with 220.50→200 with message 'Precio fijado · cliente notificado', status='quoted', persisted via GET; (5) the new admin-alert code path (orders.py L217-219 fetching admin role='admin' and calling whatsapp_service.notify_admin_logistics_priced) executes WITHOUT raising — async tasks are fire-and-forget and whatsapp_service correctly returns {sent:False, reason:'not_configured'} because Twilio env vars are intentionally absent in preview; backend logs contain ZERO errors/tracebacks after the call; (6) non-owner (admin) trying POST /orders/{id}/confirm-quote → 403; owning customer confirms → 200, status transitions 'quoted' → 'pending' (enters normal dispatch flow); (7) unit-level reload of whatsapp_service confirms is_configured()==False and both send_whatsapp() and notify_admin_logistics_priced() return {'sent': False, 'reason': 'not_configured'}.
critical_code_review_comments: orders.py L217 fetches admin via {'role':'admin'} without sort/limit — if multiple admins exist, Mongo returns an arbitrary one. For Option B the user only has ONE admin (+34612284215) so it works, but consider {'email': ADMIN_EMAIL} or sort by created_at to make it deterministic if more admins are added later.

orders.py L209 projects only {email, phone, name} for the customer but L219 then passes the partial 'customer' dict to notify_admin_logistics_priced(); whatsapp_service.notify_admin_logistics_priced safely handles missing keys via .get() with '—' fallback — clean.
whatsapp_service.send_whatsapp() correctly wraps the Twilio sync SDK in asyncio.to_thread and traps every exception, returning a structured dict. Degradation contract is solid.

All three best-effort notifications (email, customer WhatsApp, admin WhatsApp) are launched via asyncio.create_task — they correctly do NOT block the 200 response. Confirmed: PATCH responds <1s even though Twilio call would otherwise be sync.

Idempotency note (non-blocking): set-quote-price has no guard against being called twice on the same order. A second admin call resets total_amount and re-fires WhatsApp alerts. Not a bug per spec, but worth a TODO if admins might double-click.

seed_data_creation: One logistics order created during TestLogisticsQuoteFlow.test_full_flow (status: confirmed→pending after the run). Not cleaned up — left in 'pending' for traceability; can be cancelled via admin panel if needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_iter15_logistics_quote.py covers the full Camión flow + Option B admin alert. It REQUIRES env REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (has safe default to preview). The TestWhatsAppDegradation case imports whatsapp_service directly from /app/backend — depends on the preview NOT having TWILIO_* env vars set; if production tests are run, that case should be skipped or expected to actually send. For confirm-quote 403 enforcement we re-used admin_token as a non-owner — works because role check is by customer_id, not role.
rca of the issue: No bug. Option B implementation (orders.py L217-219 + whatsapp_service.notify_admin_logistics_priced) is correct and resilient. Admin phone is correctly +34612284215 in DB (read dynamically from {role:'admin'} as designed). Twilio not_configured degradation is silent, asynchronous and leaves zero traces in backend logs.
